subject: Sessions write into the tree the owner commits from
recordedOccasion: on the owner's observation that a session should hold its changes until told to release them.
severity: two findings are high. Both are silent — nothing fails, and the damage is to what the record can be trusted to mean.
scope: cross-cutting. Tracked files only; the artifact volume is out of scope and finding F6 says why.
read: `git status` and `git log` across the two concurrent sessions
all 27 existing findings bundles, checked for overlap

members.statement: Two sessions' uncommitted work interleaves in shared files, so neither can be committed alone
members.sectionHeading: F1 — two sessions' work interleaves in files neither owns alone

resolution.whatWasDone: The composition rule in §3 and docs/legend.md

members.statement: A revision's claimed validator baselines are measured on a tree containing another session's work
members.sectionHeading: F2 — a revision's validation is measured on somebody else's tree

resolution.whatWasDone: The same rule — validators run in the copy

members.statement: A session's work has no diff boundary, so the owner cannot review it as a unit
members.sectionHeading: F3 — no diff boundary, so no unit to review

resolution.whatWasDone: The same rule — the patch is the unit

members.statement: Backing out one session's change is surgical, because `git checkout` would take the other's too

resolution.whatWasDone: The same rule — declining a patch replaces reversal

members.statement: A session can amend a revision the owner has already committed
members.sectionHeading: F5 — a session can amend what the owner has already committed

resolution.whatWasDone: Numbering at apply time, and bin/check-manifest-revision.sh

members.statement: The write discipline does not distinguish the write kinds `docs/legend.md` now names
members.sectionHeading: F6 — the write kinds are named but the discipline is not

resolution.whatWasDone: A separate section in docs/legend.md, orthogonal to the categories

decisions.decision: a session composes its changes in a copy of the repository outside the connected folder, runs the validators there against its own change alone, and hands the owner a patch
decisions.sectionHeading: D1 — a session composes its changes in a copy of the repository outside the connected folder, runs the validators there against its own change alone, and hands the owner a patch

decisions.decision: an entry is composed with its number left open and numbered when the patch is applied
decisions.sectionHeading: D3 — an entry is composed with its number left open and numbered when the patch is applied

decisions.decision: the three write categories continue to answer *when* a write is allowed. *Where* it is composed becomes its own rule, applying to all three
decisions.sectionHeading: D4 — the three write categories continue to answer *when* a write is allowed. *Where* it is composed becomes its own rule, applying to all three
